note: Piece 1 of the two boys: Darrow at fourteen (Aldric a year or two older, to keep canon's ages) at a Calden muster with his father's string, which sits before Tale 1's sixteen-year-old muster without contradicting it. Feet against manners: Darrow stops the grey, Aldric stops the knight without a lie (an opinion he believes). The ride-wide signal planted as a boy's lesson; his father's 'you'll know the first time you give it' is the only line that reaches toward the ford, and says nothing of foreknowledge. Aldric's lance is named only by the tower brand. Nothing of the sister, the seal or the Oath's taking. Revised the same day for clarity: the yard's two ends set out plainly, three horses kept distinct (the black, the bay, the grey), similes thinned, and the last image made physical: Aldric steps aside as a column would, and the two boys laugh.
next_must_know: Piece 2 (the better seat): the boys know each other now; Aldric's manners and Darrow's feet are established; the signal has been shown once and must not be explained again. Keep Aldric loving and believing.

note: Piece 2: the spring after (Darrow fifteen), the water-meadows below Calden. Seat against feet: Aldric clear on the straight, Darrow level by running the grey round the thorn on foot; the fall at the cut could have been either's (the bay's feet went into the same ground and held). Aldric turns back after the fall, never before it (nothing of a heartbeat early). The copper is owed both ways and unpaid (the lesser keepsake's seed if the work runs late). The one word on the way back is not given.
next_must_know: Piece 3 (the chapel and the hand): they are friends now and ride knee to knee; a race and a copper are owed between them, unpaid. The ride-wide hand was shown in piece 1 and not used in piece 2; the last piece ends on the keepsake.
